Tips for Alice (Medic, claude-haiku-5.5): tips/tips.md
## Everyone
- Ballots are secret, so keep a notepad: for every nomination and trial, log each player's stated vote, the announced totals and your own vote, and flag any stated vote that changes or that the totals contradict (e.g. more Guilty votes than players who said Guilty). Make your own ballot match your stated read, and explain any change before the vote. (seen in 30 games)
- You can't use tokens once you're dead. Spend one-shot tokens (rig, puppet, ritual guess, shots, swaps) on the first Day or night they can change a vote or remove a threat. A puppet or doubled ballot lapses if you die that night, so spend it at least a night before a likely death. (seen in 18 games)
- A visit shows a destination, not an action: a watch can't tell protection from a frame or an attack. But if a corroborated Lookout shows X as the only unexplained visitor to a Katana victim, treat it as near-proof, and don't let 'a visit isn't an attack' acquit X. (seen in 29 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one concrete mechanical contradiction, such as a broken claim, an Evil result against a Vanilla claim, a group elimination or a lone visitor. A role-block fully explains a missing result, roles can repeat unless proven unique, and a contradiction alone doesn't separate a Yakuza from a Jester who wants the hang. (seen in 32 games)
- Before each night, write your planned target in your will. Results from the night you die never reach your will, so post every result publicly by day. (seen in 27 games)
- Answer a question about your night action in one plain sentence the first time it is asked. A dodge, or a denial you later reverse, becomes the case against you. (seen in 15 games)

## Village
- Post your role, night, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, and counterclaim at once with your full log if someone copies you. A held-back result looks retrofitted. (seen in 16 games)
- Don't hint at a power role on Day 1. Never announce tonight's target, publicly or by PM: it tells the Pharmacist whom to block and the Katana where to strike. (seen in 24 games)
- Once a player is mechanically shown Yakuza, suspect those who defended them or argued to delay. Ask for stated votes before each vote and compare them with the totals; a No on the nomination followed by Guilty once the hang is certain is the telling pattern. (seen in 27 games)
- A PM link or a pile of soft leans is a lead, never a hang: Jesters and Executioners leave PM trails on purpose. Require a mechanical result before convicting. (seen in 28 games)
- Hunt Neutral killers from Day 2. Read every cause of death: an ignite or Serial Killer attack proves that killer is alive. Keep a written suspect list (unwatched Vanilla claimants, players who survived attacks with no credible protector, unexplained visit gaps) and spend a hang on the best suspect before the endgame, because at two alive you can't hang them. (seen in 17 games)
- Before any hang, ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged: watch for self-nominations, eager-to-be-tried claims and easily disproved fake results. If you must hang a possible Jester, keep Guilty votes to a bare majority and have confirmed power roles vote Innocent. (seen in 15 games)
- Surviving an attack confirms nothing, since Arsonists and Serial Killers have Standard Defense and Jesters and Executioners have Basic. Ask the survivor what explains their Defense, and test the answer with an audit or a watch. (seen in 15 games)

## Yakuza
- Don't defend a doomed teammate unless the team's votes can actually stop the hang; otherwise vote Guilty and say so. On a likely Jester, keep some of you on Innocent, because every Guilty voter is in the revenge draw. (seen in 34 games)
- Never PM teammates by day: an Eavesdropper or Wiretap reads it, and a visible PM triangle becomes the town's lead. Plan in night chat. (seen in 30 games)
- Agree a fake claim in night chat before Day 2 that fits your token count and real visits. Never claim a Yakuza-only role or a unique role, and never switch claims once cornered. (seen in 18 games)
- Every member submits the agreed Katana holder and target every night; with two Yakuza, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 19 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member, and move it the same night once a Lookout or Tracker names the holder. After a failed attack, remove the protector instead of retrying. (seen in 21 games)

## Neutral
- If you survive an attack, nobody else knows you were targeted, so don't announce it. If you must explain it, pick one claim at once and keep it. (seen in 6 games)

## Sheriff
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, so a Not Evil result on a suspected attacker clears nothing; say so when you post it. Once only one Yakuza can be alive, no Not Evil result clears anyone. (seen in 16 games)

## Medic
- Your free Standard protection stops the Katana: use it on vocal analysts and claimed investigators, and rotate rather than follow a predictable pattern. Self-protect with a token the night you claim, and never say you 'confirmed' a save, since you get no feedback. (seen in 21 games)

## Vigilante
- Shoot on a lead, not proof: a claim conflict, an Evil result against an unverifiable claim, or a defender of an exposed Yakuza. Dying with all your tokens is the usual failure. A failed Basic shot hints at innate Defense, so post it. (seen in 11 games)

## Clerk
- Rig a Day when a townie can win a nomination but not a Guilty majority, never when a teammate is the likely nominee. On the rigged trial, teammates vote Innocent, because a small Guilty total exposes them. (seen in 18 games)

## Smuggler
- A swap moves exactly the actions aimed at the two swapped players, so don't veto it out of fear. To beat a Medic, aim the Katana at a decoy and swap the decoy with your real target. To dodge a check, swap yourself with a Villager. Never swap the target unless you mean to move the kill, and have a cover ready for both swap visits. (seen in 7 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 or more players are doused, or 2 if you're being questioned. Douse players likely to survive, not today's hang targets. (seen in 12 games)

Tips for Frank (Fixer, claude-haiku-5.5): tips/tips.md
## Everyone
- Ballots are secret, so keep a notepad: for every nomination and trial, log each player's stated vote, the announced totals and your own vote, and flag any stated vote that changes or that the totals contradict (e.g. more Guilty votes than players who said Guilty). Make your own ballot match your stated read, and explain any change before the vote. (seen in 30 games)
- You can't use tokens once you're dead. Spend one-shot tokens (rig, puppet, ritual guess, shots, swaps) on the first Day or night they can change a vote or remove a threat. A puppet or doubled ballot lapses if you die that night, so spend it at least a night before a likely death. (seen in 18 games)
- A visit shows a destination, not an action: a watch can't tell protection from a frame or an attack. But if a corroborated Lookout shows X as the only unexplained visitor to a Katana victim, treat it as near-proof, and don't let 'a visit isn't an attack' acquit X. (seen in 29 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one concrete mechanical contradiction, such as a broken claim, an Evil result against a Vanilla claim, a group elimination or a lone visitor. A role-block fully explains a missing result, roles can repeat unless proven unique, and a contradiction alone doesn't separate a Yakuza from a Jester who wants the hang. (seen in 32 games)
- Before each night, write your planned target in your will. Results from the night you die never reach your will, so post every result publicly by day. (seen in 27 games)
- Answer a question about your night action in one plain sentence the first time it is asked. A dodge, or a denial you later reverse, becomes the case against you. (seen in 15 games)

## Village
- Post your role, night, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, and counterclaim at once with your full log if someone copies you. A held-back result looks retrofitted. (seen in 16 games)
- Don't hint at a power role on Day 1. Never announce tonight's target, publicly or by PM: it tells the Pharmacist whom to block and the Katana where to strike. (seen in 24 games)
- Once a player is mechanically shown Yakuza, suspect those who defended them or argued to delay. Ask for stated votes before each vote and compare them with the totals; a No on the nomination followed by Guilty once the hang is certain is the telling pattern. (seen in 27 games)
- A PM link or a pile of soft leans is a lead, never a hang: Jesters and Executioners leave PM trails on purpose. Require a mechanical result before convicting. (seen in 28 games)
- Hunt Neutral killers from Day 2. Read every cause of death: an ignite or Serial Killer attack proves that killer is alive. Keep a written suspect list (unwatched Vanilla claimants, players who survived attacks with no credible protector, unexplained visit gaps) and spend a hang on the best suspect before the endgame, because at two alive you can't hang them. (seen in 17 games)
- Before any hang, ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged: watch for self-nominations, eager-to-be-tried claims and easily disproved fake results. If you must hang a possible Jester, keep Guilty votes to a bare majority and have confirmed power roles vote Innocent. (seen in 15 games)
- Surviving an attack confirms nothing, since Arsonists and Serial Killers have Standard Defense and Jesters and Executioners have Basic. Ask the survivor what explains their Defense, and test the answer with an audit or a watch. (seen in 15 games)

## Yakuza
- Don't defend a doomed teammate unless the team's votes can actually stop the hang; otherwise vote Guilty and say so. On a likely Jester, keep some of you on Innocent, because every Guilty voter is in the revenge draw. (seen in 34 games)
- Never PM teammates by day: an Eavesdropper or Wiretap reads it, and a visible PM triangle becomes the town's lead. Plan in night chat. (seen in 30 games)
- Agree a fake claim in night chat before Day 2 that fits your token count and real visits. Never claim a Yakuza-only role or a unique role, and never switch claims once cornered. (seen in 18 games)
- Every member submits the agreed Katana holder and target every night; with two Yakuza, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 19 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member, and move it the same night once a Lookout or Tracker names the holder. After a failed attack, remove the protector instead of retrying. (seen in 21 games)

## Neutral
- If you survive an attack, nobody else knows you were targeted, so don't announce it. If you must explain it, pick one claim at once and keep it. (seen in 6 games)

- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, so a Not Evil result on a suspected attacker clears nothing; say so when you post it. Once only one Yakuza can be alive, no Not Evil result clears anyone. (seen in 16 games)

Task prompt
It is Day 2, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 2.50; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; leave it "" to keep it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; leave it "" to keep it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

It is Day 2, round 4 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 4.72; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 4, 1.50x; next round 2.00x):
   10 words: public 1.75, private 0.44
   25 words: public 2.15, private 0.54
   50 words: public 2.84, private 0.71
  100 words: public 4.38, private 1.09
  200 words: public 8.00, private 2.00
  400 words: public 17.50, private 4.38
  800 words: public 45.50, private 11.38
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; leave it "" to keep it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; leave it "" to keep it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.50 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 7, 3.00x; next round 3.50x):
   10 words: public 3.51, private 0.88
   25 words: public 4.30, private 1.07
   50 words: public 5.69, private 1.42
  100 words: public 8.75, private 2.19
  200 words: public 16.00, private 4.00
  400 words: public 35.00, private 8.75
  800 words: public 91.00, private 22.75
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; leave it "" to keep it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; leave it "" to keep it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 3.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

It is Day 2, round 8 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 5.29; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important.   100 words: public 10.21, private 2.55
  200 words: public 18.67, private 4.67

A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.

Task prompt
It is Day 3, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 3.58; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; leave it "" to keep it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; leave it "" to keep it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

Task prompt
It is Day 3, round 2 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 7.03; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices during this trial (1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
This is a trial turn: prices are 1x whatever the round, and you also get a trial-only budget of 2.00, spent before your regular budget. Unspent trial budget is lost when this turn ends, but don't speak just to use it up: say nothing if you have nothing to add.
Your public message this turn is free up to 150 words; beyond that you pay only for the extra length.
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; leave it "" to keep it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; leave it "" to keep it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You are on trial. Defend yourself; you speak first. This turn is only for discussion: after everyone has spoken, all players vote Guilty/Innocent in a separate, simultaneous vote.

Outside log review (rules and bugs)
Review: medium, player confusionOn Days 2 and 3, several Village players (Bob, Dave, Heidi, Alice) said Heidi's Insomniac log showed 'a real Sheriff visit on Frank'. The Insomniac learns only the roles of visitors, not their targets. Frank and Grace pointed this out during the trial, and Heidi then admitted it. Some votes were justified with this mistaken reading.
Review: low, player confusionPlayers misread the Auditor's scope. On Day 2 Carol said 'anyone who casts a nomination vote today will be checked', and on Day 3 Erin asked Carol to 'post your audit on each Yes voter'. The Auditor audits only one player per night. Carol's post-game feedback also said the auditor result's scope was hard to pin down.
Review: low, prompt problemCarol's debrief said the speaking-budget rules were hard to pin down and asked for a worked example or a per-turn budget readout. This suggests the players' budget information is unclear.
Game over
